selfplay_seconds.description: Wall time of the epoch's self-play, compiling included the first time a search plays. With the run's other *_seconds, what to compare runs by at equal GPU time.

train_seconds.description: Wall time of the epoch's training, every network that trains (with growth, each network's own is <name>/train_seconds), compiling included the first time.

test_seconds.description: Wall time of the epoch's tests, every network's that trains (with growth, each network's own is <name>/test_seconds).

epoch_seconds.description: Wall time of the whole epoch: self-play, training, tests and checkpoints.

run_seconds.description: Wall time of the run's training loop so far, startup and compiling included, carried over when a run is continued from a saved state (not when it's forked).

selfplay_evals.description: Positions the network evaluated in the epoch's self-play: search cycles times environments, since every environment pays every cycle (waiting ones included). With growth, also <name>/selfplay_evals for the network playing. Times a benchmark of the network's forward pass at self-play's batch, the epoch's self-play compute.

*/selfplay_evals.description: With growth: selfplay_evals, logged under the name of the network that played.

train_samples.description: Samples trained on this epoch, by every network that trains (each a forward and a backward pass); with growth, each network's own is <name>/train_samples. Times a benchmark of a training step per sample, the epoch's training compute.

*/train_samples.description: With growth: the samples this network trained on this epoch.

growth_playing.description: With growth: the index of the network self-play played with this epoch (the run's first network is 0).

growth_gap.description: With growth: the next network's switch metric (e.g. engine_value_mse), averaged over the rule's window, minus the playing network's. The next takes over once it's at or below 0, after its minimum epochs.

growth_switch.description: With growth: the index of the network that takes over self-play, logged at the epoch whose results made it; it plays from the next epoch.

growth_guard_gap.description: With growth and a guard: as growth_gap, of the guard's metric (e.g. engine_value_mse when the rule compares the training loss). The next must be at or below 0 on it too to take over.

growth_caught_up.description: With growth: 1 once the next network has caught up (trained its minimum epochs, growth_gap at or below 0, or below minus the rule's margin of the playing network's metric, and no worse on its guard), else 0. A manual rule only reports it: the next takes over when a controller branches the run with it playing.

loss.description: The loss training minimizes, averaged over the epoch's training steps. With the default loss function, policy_loss + value_loss.

policy_loss.description: Cross-entropy of the network's policy against the search's policy target (its visit counts, or Gumbel MuZero's completed-Q policy), averaged over the epoch's training steps.

value_loss.description: Half the squared error of the network's value against its target (the game's outcome for the player to move, mixed with the search's value with value_target_q), averaged over the epoch's training steps.

policy_target_entropy.description: Entropy of the search's policy targets (nats), averaged over the epoch's training steps: the part of policy_loss no network can lower. It changes with the search and the target (more sims, a kept tree, completed-Q), so compare policy_kl, not policy_loss, across runs that differ in those.

policy_kl.description: policy_loss - policy_target_entropy: the KL divergence from the search's policy targets to the network's policy (nats), averaged over the epoch's training steps. How well the network fits its targets, whatever they are.

heldout_policy_kl.description: distill.py: KL divergence from the search's policies to the network's on games neither it nor its teacher trained on.

heldout_value_mse_z.description: distill.py: the value's MSE against the game's outcome on games neither the network nor its teacher trained on. Compare with probe_value_mse_z for memorisation; it misleads across value targets, since a target's calibration moves it without changing strength.

heldout_value_mse_teacher.description: distill.py: the value's MSE against the teacher's on games neither trained on.

probe_*.description: distill.py: as heldout_*, on a fixed sample of the positions the network trains on.

train_*.description: distill.py: the training step's metric, from the last step before this measurement.

minutes.description: distill.py: training time so far, not counting loading.

learning_rate.description: The learning rate, averaged over the epoch's training steps. Logged when the optimizer schedules it.

lr_plateau_improvement.description: With a learning rate that drops on plateaus: how much the training loss fell over the rule's window of epochs at the current rate, by minus the slope of a least-squares line through the epochs' losses, times their number. The rate drops when it's under the rule's threshold.

lr_drop.description: With a learning rate that drops on plateaus: the rate it dropped to, logged at the epoch whose loss made it drop. The next epoch trains at it.

lr_last_plateau.description: With a learning rate that drops on plateaus: the last rate, logged at the epoch it plateaued. Training stops there if the rule says to.

weight_decay.description: The weight decay, averaged over the epoch's training steps. Logged when the optimizer schedules it.

weight_norm.description: ||w||: the norm of the weights weight decay applies to (not biases or BatchNorm scales and offsets).

grad_norm.description: The global norm of the loss's gradient, over all trained parameters, averaged over the epoch's training steps.

grad_norm_max.description: The largest global gradient norm of the epoch's training steps. A step far above the median (grad_norm_spike) is the usual warning before training blows up; an epoch's mean hides it.

grad_norm_median.description: The median global gradient norm of the epoch's training steps.

grad_norm_spike.description: grad_norm_max / grad_norm_median: how far the epoch's worst gradient stood above its typical one. Above about 10 is a warning sign.

loss_spike.description: The largest training step's loss over the median step's, this epoch: a sudden bad step that a mean over the epoch hides.

nonfinite_steps.description: Training steps this epoch whose loss or gradient wasn't finite (NaN or infinite). Should always be 0.

update_ratio.description: ||update|| / ||w||: an optimizer step's size relative to the weights it moves, over the weights weight decay applies to. Under BatchNorm this, not the learning rate, says how fast a convolution moves; with AdamW it settles near sqrt(2 * learning rate * weight decay).

gns_tr_sigma.description: With gradient accumulation: the trace of the per-sample gradient covariance, tr(Sigma), estimated from the micro-batches' gradients against their mean's (McCandlish et al. 2018), averaged over the epoch's training steps.

gns_grad_sq.description: With gradient accumulation: the true gradient's squared norm, |G|^2, estimated from the micro-batches' gradients against their mean's, averaged over the epoch's training steps. At weights that jitter it includes their pull back to the centre.

gns_noise_scale.description: With gradient accumulation: the gradient noise scale tr(Sigma) / |G|^2, the batch size at which a step is half signal. It grows as a network converges. Measured at the weights training moves, it underestimates when they jitter.

gns_signal_share.description: With gradient accumulation: B / (B + noise scale), the share of a training step at its batch size B that is signal rather than noise.

gns_avg_tr_sigma.description: With --noise-measure: tr(Sigma), the per-sample gradient covariance's trace, at the self-play weight average, from a few micro-batches.

gns_avg_grad_sq.description: With --noise-measure: the true gradient's squared norm at the self-play weight average, where the jitter's pull back to the centre doesn't inflate it.

gns_avg_noise_scale.description: With --noise-measure: the gradient noise scale at the self-play weight average, tr(Sigma) / |G|^2: the batch size at which a step is half signal.

lr_scale.description: With a learning rate drop (--lr-drop): the factor this epoch's updates were scaled by, below 1 once the network has played its epochs at the full rate.

fresh_policy_kl_raw.description: The playing network's policy KL on the positions its self-play just stored, before training on them, at its raw weights.

fresh_policy_kl_avg.description: The same at its self-play weight average.

fresh_policy_kl_gap.description: fresh_policy_kl_raw minus fresh_policy_kl_avg: what the step's jitter costs the policy on new data. Large means a learning rate drop should pay (a stalled Othello 12x144: 0.036, a cooled 4x32: 0.003).

fresh_value_loss_raw.description: The playing network's value loss on the positions its self-play just stored, before training on them, at its raw weights.

fresh_value_loss_avg.description: The same at its self-play weight average.

fresh_value_loss_gap.description: fresh_value_loss_raw minus fresh_value_loss_avg: what the step's jitter costs the value on new data.

tree_batch_fraction.description: The fraction of each training batch that is search tree positions rather than played positions.

tree_buffer_samples.description: Search tree positions in the replay buffer that training can sample.

moves.description: Self-play moves played this epoch, in all environments.

episodes.description: Self-play games that ended this epoch.

buffer_capacity.description: The replay buffer's capacity, positions per self-play environment: the replay window training samples from.

buffer_samples.description: Experiences in the replay buffer that training can sample.

buffer_distinct_positions.description: Distinct observations among the replay buffer's experiences, those a data transform maps to one another (e.g. a board and its rotations) counting as one.

buffer_distinct_fraction.description: buffer_distinct_positions / buffer_samples. A fall means self-play is collapsing into the same few games.

episode_draw.description: The fraction of the self-play games that ended this epoch that were drawn.

episode_*.description: An episode_metrics_fn metric, averaged over the self-play games that ended this epoch.

tree_positions.description: Search tree positions stored this epoch, besides the positions played.

tree_positions_per_move.description: Search tree positions stored per self-play move.

tree_mean_visits.description: The mean visits of the search tree positions stored this epoch.

search_iterations.description: MCTS iterations a self-play search runs, per move (their mean, with playout cap randomization).

cycles_per_move.description: Search cycles (the root's evaluation and each iteration) per self-play move played, counting cycles spent waiting for a move to be played: self-play's compute per move.

full_searches.description: Self-play searches whose moves were played this epoch and whose positions are stored for training (with playout cap randomization, the full ones; otherwise every search): the epoch's new training positions, counting those of games later cut off.

fast_searches.description: Self-play searches whose moves were played this epoch without storing their positions (playout cap randomization's fast searches).

*_search_cycles.description: Search cycles (the root's evaluation and each iteration) a full_ or fast_ search took on average, counting those it waited for its move to be played.

*_search_stopped.description: Share of full_ or fast_ searches done before their iterations were up, e.g. stopped by smart pruning.

*_search_inherited_visits.description: Visits a full_ or fast_ search's root had from earlier searches as it started (the subtree kept from the last move's tree; a root searched from scratch counts 1), on average: what smart pruning on earlier moves' searches leaves the next search.

*_level*_sims*_game.description: A game the network, searching sims iterations a move, played against the engine at that level, with its opening.

*_level*_sims*_last*_se.description: The standard error of the mean score of the last networks against the engine (the _last* metric): how much it would move with other openings, each game's result averaged over the networks first, since they all play the same games.

*_level*_sims*_last*.description: The mean score against the engine at that level, searching sims iterations a move, of the networks after each of the run's last epochs (as many as the suffix says), logged at the last: steadier than one network's, which drifts from its neighbours' by more than the games' own noise.

*_level*_sims*_se.description: The standard error of the score against the engine at that level: how much it would move with other openings. About 0.02 for 512 games.

*_level*_sims*_win.description: The fraction of the games against the engine at that level that the network won.

*_level*_sims*_draw.description: The fraction of the games against the engine at that level that were drawn.

*_level*_sims*_loss.description: The fraction of the games against the engine at that level that the network lost.

*_level*_sims*.description: The network's score against the engine at that level, searching sims iterations a move, its search tree kept between moves and no root noise (a win 1, a draw 0.5, a loss 0), in games from varied openings each played with both colors: the same games for every network, given the openings.

*_game.description: A test game of the tester it's named after, with what each move's search explored.

*_avg_outcome.description: The network's mean outcome in test games (a win 1, a draw 0, a loss -1) against the opponent it's named after; for a TwoPlayerTester, against the best network so far.

*_rung.description: Ladder rungs beaten so far: the next test plays the rung above.

*_score.description: The ladder's score against this rung's opponent (a win 1, a draw 0.5, a loss 0). Past promote_score, the ladder moves up.

*_win_rate.description: The fraction of the test games against this opponent the network won.

*_loss_rate.description: The fraction of the test games against this opponent the network lost.

edax_seconds.description: Seconds the games against Edax took (every level, compiling the search included the first time), played between epochs: take them out of the run's wall time to get its training time.

mohex_seconds.description: Seconds the games against MoHex took (every level, compiling the search included the first time), played between epochs: take them out of the run's wall time to get its training time.

egaroucid_seconds.description: Seconds the games against Egaroucid took (every level, compiling the search included the first time), played between epochs: take them out of the run's wall time to get its training time.

solver_seconds.description: Seconds the games against the Connect Four solver took (every level, compiling the search included the first time), played between epochs: take them out of the run's wall time to get its training time.

*_seconds.description: Seconds the ladder's games against this rung took, compiling included the first time it's played.

outcome_top1*.description: How often the network's most likely move keeps the game's result under perfect play, on the solver-labelled positions (a suffix names a group: critical is the positions where the result depends on the move). No search.

outcome_exp_regret*.description: How much of the game's result the network's policy gives up under perfect play, expected over its policy, on the solver-labelled positions (a win to a draw is 1, to a loss 2; a suffix names a group). No search.

outcome_regret*.description: How much of the game's result the network's most likely move gives up under perfect play, on the solver-labelled positions (a win to a draw is 1, to a loss 2; a suffix names a group). No search.

outcome_value_mse*.description: (value - z)^2 of the network's value, z the game's true result under perfect play (+1, 0 or -1), on the solver-labelled positions (a suffix names a group). The same as engine_value_mse. No search.

outcome_value_sign*.description: How often the network's value has the sign of the game's true result under perfect play, over the solver-labelled positions that aren't draws (a suffix names a group). The same as engine_value_sign. No search.

*_top1*.description: How often the network's most likely action is one of the engine's best, on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a game phase: opening, midgame or endgame). No search.

*_exp_regret*.description: The score the network's policy gives up against the engine's best action, expected over its policy, on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a group). Less noisy than regret, but it also measures how sharp the policy is: compare it only between runs with the same search and policy target (across them, use regret and value_mse). No search.

*_regret*.description: The score the network's most likely action gives up against the engine's best, on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a group). No search.

*_value_mse*.description: (value - z)^2 of the network's value, z the outcome the engine predicts (+1, 0 or -1), on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a group). No search.

*_value_sign*.description: How often the network's value has the sign of the outcome the engine predicts, over the engine-labelled positions it doesn't call a draw (a suffix names a group). No search.

avg*/*.description: With weight averages: the metric of the network's weights averaged over about the epochs the prefix names (avg4: 4), scored as the network's own is (see Trainer's averages); the metric is as it is described without the prefix.

*/avg*/*.description: With growth and weight averages: one network's avg<horizon>/<metric>, as avg*/* describes.

*/*.description: With growth: one network's own metric, <its name>/<metric>; the metric is as it is described without the prefix. The network playing self-play also logs its metrics without it.
